summary: Every student takes the IDEAS seminars and the research methods core, picks a base area (CTE, DAPS or SHIPS), and reaches 135 graduate units. LSTD and RILE are optional cross-area specializations on top of the base area: LSTD needs nine quarters of EDUC 291 and proficiency, shown by courses or prior work your advisor accepts, in research methods, design, learning, technology perspectives and disciplinary learning, and RILE needs six quarters of EDUC 489 and five distribution courses that may also count elsewhere. In SHIPS you choose one program option (an HSS discipline, one of the IDE areas, or a dual specialization), and Education Data Science needs one course in three of its five tracks. The research methods course of your choice, the advanced methods course, the master's or minor outside the GSE, the 3.0 GPA, transfer units, the research apprenticeship with a faculty member, at least three TAships (from the Fall 2024 cohort), reviews, qualifying papers, candidacy, the proposal, the oral exam and the dissertation are checked by your advisor and the department.

replace.name: Data Science Specializations
replace.desc:
Data Science Specializations
Students will also complete data science specializations in their course of study.
Students will fulfill this requirement by completing at least 1 course in 3 of the 5 available tracks listed below.
The areas of concentration that will be offered are:
• Natural Language Processing
• Network Science
• Experiments & Causal Methods
• Measurement
• Learning Analytics
These courses are established courses at Stanford University and will allow for inter-professional education of GSE students and graduate students from other departments. We anticipate that these tracks may change overtime with advances in data science.
